A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same e-GAI study and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–C. Corresponding equations, proofs, experiments, tables and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B–C report original simulations, parameter and runtime studies, and analyses of NYC taxi and Nasdaq data.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Gaussian and AR(1) simulations, taxi anomaly detection and financial-bubble detection.

M1.justification: The e-GAI estimators, risk-aversion updates, e-LORD/e-SAFFRON algorithms, memory variants and p-value adaptations are unchanged. Section 5.3 rephrases the existing likelihood-ratio normalization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use correlated Gaussian simulations, time-varying AR(1) simulations, NYC taxi anomalies and Nasdaq bubble dating. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: e-LOND, LORD++, SAFFRON and SupLORD, plus mem-LORD++ in the long-term study. The additional taxi comparisons in Appendix C.3 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Data generation, calibration samples, metrics and parameter settings are unchanged. For example, taxi calibration still uses the first 2,000 observations, with testing levels 0.1 for e-value methods and 0.2 for p-value methods.

E4.justification: Appendices B–C retain the allocation-parameter sensitivity analyses, dependence comparisons, runtime study and long-term mem-FDR experiments. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors in the simulation figures and 100 repetitions for Tables 3–4. Repetition information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains FDP estimates 0.085, 0.087 and 0.061 and discovery counts 47, 46 and 33 for e-LORD, e-SAFFRON and e-LOND. Other results, including appendix tables and plots, are unchanged. Figure 3's added shading displays existing detections.

T1.justification: The assumptions, mathematical definitions, theorems and proofs in the main text and Appendices A–B are unchanged. Corrections to the wording of conditional super-uniformity leave the equations and mathematical reasoning intact.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and summary retain the same claims about conditional FDR control, dynamic allocation, power, memory extensions and applicability to p-values.

C2.justification: v1's Figure 2 caption attributes e-SAFFRON's power loss to few large e-values. v2 moves the explanation to Table 2 and instead attributes it to few true alternatives. This changes the stated explanation without adding supporting analysis; other interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Code-access information, R packages, hyperparameters, calibration instructions and Appendix B's computational formulas remain unchanged. The rewritten normalization sentence in Section 5.3 supplies no new implementation information.

R1.justification: No cited works are added or removed. The positioning relative to GAI, e-LOND and earlier p-value methods, including the connections in Appendix B.5, is unchanged.

P1.justification: Scattered grammar and terminology corrections accompany limited rewrites of the real-data descriptions. Section 5.2 corrects 'black squares' to 'red squares' when referring to Figure 2. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3 adds red shading around existing e-LOND detections and adjusts annotation placement. The power explanation moves, with revised wording, from Figure 2's caption to Table 2's caption. Other changes are limited to captions and local text flow.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the Figure 2 marker-color reference and adds the red e-LOND region already described by Figure 3's caption, improving consistency between text and graphics. Copyediting also improves readability. The revised power explanation adds no evidence, and the methods, proofs and experimental support remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
